Goal 1: Graduates will be prepared to enter research-focused graduate programs based on their knowledge of empirically- supported psychological processes and how to apply this knowledge to promote health and welfare.

Goal 3: Graduates will be able to work ethically in settings that emphasize diversity and global thinking.
The BS in Psychology is described to students as a program that focuses on the empirical and methodological aspects of psychology, that emphasizes math, science, and research methods in creating and applying psychological knowledge, and that includes a requirement in hands on research experience.

Mark Robbins A BS in psychology prepares students for a wide variety of career options.
According to the website of the American Psychological Association ( https://www.apa.org/ed/precollege/psn/2018/01/bachelors-degree ), about 25 percent of psychology baccalaureates go to graduate school in psychology, about 18 percent go on for more education but not in psychology, and 57 percent are workforce graduates (Lin, Christidis & Stamm, 2017).
The BS degree prepares graduates especially well to apply to doctoral or other research-oriented advanced degrees in Psychology or other fields.

For those who do not wish to obtain an advanced degree, there are many job opportunities.
The above referenced website lists 70 job titles that students with a BS in Psychology are prepared for.
The BS degree with its focus on methodology, scientific writing, and statistical analysis especially trains graduates for any type of position requiring analytic, scientific writing, or data analytic skills, such as data base design analyst, research assistant, systems analyst, technical writer, information specialist, or data base manager.
A number of these occupations are considered high impact jobs in RI.
The Occupational Outlook Handbook of the Bureau of Labor ( https://www.bls.gov/ooh/field-of- degree/psychology/psychology-field-of-degree.htm ) indicates that the median salary for those with a degree in Psychology is $50,000 and that 60% are employed in occupations requiring at least a bachelor's degree.
Many department faculty offer students the opportunity to serve as undergraduate teaching assistants for course credit.
There are no paid undergraduate assistantships.
Graduate teaching assistantships are offered to assist instructors with PSY 200, PSY 301, and PSY 435.

Among peer institutions (UMass, UConn, UVM, UNH, U of Maine, and U of Delaware) BS degrees in Psychology are offered by three (UMASS, UCONN, and UVM).
The University of Delaware offers a BS in Neuroscience but not Psychology.
UNH and U of Maine offer only BA programs.
It does not make URI unique in our region to offer this degree, but if we did not offer it, we would not be keeping up with the more research/science oriented institutions in our region.
There is a trend among peer institutions to emphasize the scientific basis of psychology, which the proposed changes to the program are designed to accomplish.
